lots.working: Keep: the literal lowest sale ($4) is a freak, so I used the lower quartile of the last 3 months (about $30 to $35) as the lowest representative same-item price: $30 / 1.198 = $25.04, round down to $25. Flip: likely resale about $50 hammer if re-auctioned at Gowans (no retail timber source available), less an assumed 15% vendor commission (Gowans vendor rate not checked) = $42.50, no postage (bulky, local pickup), / 2.396 = $17.74, round down to $15. Flipping is not realistic at these numbers.
lots.confidence_reason: Huge pool of same-title Gowans sales opened and recomputed, but no mark to read, species not provable from the photo and slab size/thickness unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher entry 2's claim that a handful of single Huon slab lots reached $300 to $750 hammer: not supported, the exact-title maximum is $180; the higher figures belong to other titles (logs, furniture). Researcher UNSOLD entry dropped: only 2 zero-price past lots in the window, not 1 in 40, and the API gives no reserve or last bid, so it carries no price. Researcher entries 1 to 3 restated with my own recomputed figures from the same URL (their medians of $55 checked out).
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Chalk 1117 9/10/26 and a 1117 sticker. Plain pale tan face with faint fiddle-like ripples, no birdseye, no visible growth-ring detail. Bark along the right edge, broken live edge on the left, a rotten notch at the base. Colour is paler and less yellow than typical Huon pine; species cannot be confirmed from the photo.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, some edge decay at the base notch, otherwise sound looking. Thickness not visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of lot 1117, and is the timber confirmed Huon pine (smell or vendor source)? Any rot or splits on the back?
